<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916678_theRebbe_290" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916678_theRebbe_290__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that there are nations of the world who completely deny the existence of G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">For we find that the nations of the world deny the existence of G-d entirely.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that this question is not on the maamar itself, but on the Sages' statement that is its foundation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now this question is not on the maamar,</t>
    <t s="1">but rather on the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="2">(at the end of Menachos)</t>
    <t s="3">who called Him "the G-d of the gods"</t>
    <t s="4">(and it is learned there from a verse — "From the rising of the sun to its setting" etc.),</t>
    <t s="5">which statement of our Sages is the foundation explained in the maamar.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the clarification is understood from the Tzemach Tzedek's Sefer HaMitzvos, and is not the place to elaborate.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the explanation of this is understood from what is written in the Sefer HaMitzvos of the Tzemach Tzedek, at the end of the mitzvah of the Unity of Hashem; see there.</t>
    <t s="1">And elsewhere is not the place.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
